moat_against: Givaudan is the clear leader and dsm-firmenich strengthened by its 2023 merger — IFF is not the share-gainer
Large FMCG customers hold bargaining power; pricing has largely been cost pass-through
Repeated goodwill impairments (FY2022-FY2025) prove acquired earnings power was overpaid for and decayed
Fragrance-business antitrust investigations add legal cost and headline risk
Underlying category grows only mid-single digits, capping compounding
moat_for: Top-four F&F oligopoly — top four houses hold over 50% of the global market
Proprietary formulation libraries and confidential co-development embed IFF in customers' finished products
Global scale across taste, scent and biosciences smaller houses cannot match
Continuing business still growing — Q2 2026 continuing sales ~+6% currency-neutral, FY2026 EBITDA guided +4-8%
moat_justification: Top-four global F&F oligopoly seat with proprietary formulation libraries and confidential co-development embedded in customers' products, but IFF has not converted the seat into durable returns: repeated goodwill impairments (including Food Ingredients in FY2025), a stronger leader in Givaudan, large FMCG customers with bargaining power, and only mid-single-digit category growth. Moderate/narrow moat, CAP 8.5 years.
name: INTERNATIONAL FLAVORS & FRAGRANCES INC
one_liner: Real top-four F&F franchise, moat 5/10, but owner's earnings are trough-level ($1.76/share TTM) against heavy net debt — at $90.29 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 4.6%, weighted IV@15% $14.92); it would need to trade near $14.92 to clear the hurdle on this screen.
